rationale: This is the archived gen-8 "Smooth-Earnings Cash-to-Accrual Substitution" signal with one extra profitability indicator bolted on — a cosmetic sample filter rather than a new mechanism, and it will mostly trim coverage of an already-narrow qualifying set.

Internally consistent and the persistence idea is defensible, but three-period smoothing of both legs of the identical archived winner is a standard time-averaging tweak, not a substantively different construct.

Replacing the two-flow conjunction with a stock-composition drift measure is a genuinely different construction of the mechanism with better continuity and coverage, though reviewers should watch that it does not collapse into a mechanical change-in-cash / asset-growth proxy.

Swapping the earnings-smoothness gate for the durable-margin gate is economically coherent and the sign logic is correct, but it is a conditioning-variable substitution on an existing winner rather than a new economic channel, and the hard indicator gate again discards continuous information.

Another gate swap on the same substitution score, and the margin-improvement indicator combined with a working-capital funding score is very close to the already-archived "Margin Improvement Funding Test," so incremental information content is likely small.

This is a linear blend of two archived signals whose components share the same dominant term (DELTA(act) − DELTA(che)), so it double-counts a single accrual channel and functions as an ensemble rather than a testable new hypothesis.
